definitions.name: Access Code
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 1 Name: Access Code 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 12 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to 12 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies data that must be dialed prior to dialing the phone 
number in the Telephone Table Load Response. 
 Examples. PBX access codes 
   Codes for disabling custom calling features 
Processing Rules: If Access Code information is not necessary, the dial string 
contains neither this element nor the Pause Indicator that 
immediately follows it; however, this element may be used to 
indicate a much longer than standard pause for use with phone 
systems that are slow to provide a dial tone.  In these cases, one 
or more B characters may be inserted in this element.  Each one 
should be interpreted as a 1-second pause. 
Valid Codes/Values:  Any number 
    B

Representation: 
 Non-TransArmor—Initial Transaction—Request: 
 Format: 123456789012nn…nn 
 Where 123456789012nn…nn = a variable length (up to 24 alphanumeric 
bytes) Account Number. 
 Non-TransArmor—Initial Transaction—Response: 
 Format: 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn 
 Where 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn = a fixed length (25 alphanumeric bytes) 
Account Number. 
 Non-TransArmor— Subsequent Transaction —Request: 
 Format: 123456789012nn…nn 
 Where 123456789012nn…nn = a variable length (up to 24 alphanumeric 
bytes) Account Number. 
 Non-TransArmor— Subsequent Transaction —Response: 
 Format: 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn 
 Where 123456789012nnnnnnnnnnnnn = a fixed length (25 alphanumeric bytes) 
Account Number. 
 TransArmor – All Messages: 
 For all TransArmor formatting of the Account Number field, see Appendix AA. 
TransArmor Processing Considerations. 
 
Purpose: Non-TransArmor:  Identifies the card or account. 
 TransArmor (Either Encryption Method):  Identifies the 25-byte 
TransArmor header plus the 400-byte EDATA block that contains 
the encrypted/unencrypted information that identifies the account 
for TransArmor. 
  
 
Processing Rules: For non-TransArmor and TransArmor Token Only, the POS 
device maintains the card’s Account Number until it receives a 
response from the host. 
 For TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization, the POS 
device must not maintain the card’s Account Number after the 
initial card swipe. 
 For Non-TransArmor and TransArmor, if the Account Number is 
obtained from a Track 2 card reader, instead of being manually 
keyed, the Account Number and Card Discretionary Block Data 
should consist of all data read from the card between, but not 
including, the Start Sentinel and End Sentinel.  Account Number is 
considered the data before the = character, and Card 
Discretionary Block Data is considered the data after the = 
character.  The = character is used instead of a Field Separator. 
 For Non-TransArmor and TransArmor, if the Account Number is 
obtained from a Track 1 card reader (credit cards only), instead of

Discretionary Block Data should consist of all unaltered data read

first ^ character, and Card Discretionary Block Data is considered 
the data after the first ^ character.  The ^ character is used instead

 For TransArmor (Either Encryption Method) – Account Number

Note: Track data placed in the combined data elements of

Real Time Account Updater: 
When a merchant receives Account Updater Card Number (New 
PAN) in the original transaction response in the Real Time 
Account Updater Response Segment – Segment 155, the 
merchant can send either the new PAN or the original PAN in the 
‘Follow-on’ transactions in this Account Number field. 
When a merchant receives Account Updater TransArmor Token 
(New TransArmor Token) in the original transaction response in 
the Real Time Account Updater Response Segment – Segment 
155, the merchant can send either the new TransArmor token or 
the original TransArmor token in the ‘Follow-on’ transactions in 
this Account Number field as TAP request. 
In the event of a ‘Retry’ of a ‘Follow-on’ transaction (Reversals, 
Completions, Cancellations, Void of Merchandise Return, and 
Timeout reversals) by the merchant, the merchant should use the 
same credentials for the retry as were used in the initial attempt.  
Refer to Appendix AD – Real Time Account Updater for more 
details. 
 
 
Valid Codes/Values: Credit, debit, and EBT cards:  Please refer to the most recent

Reference Manual. 
Fleet cards:  Please refer to the most recent version of

Specifications. 
Stored Value cards:  The length of the Account Number should

definitions.name: Approval Number
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 5 Name: Approval Number 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 6 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of six alphanumeric characters; space-filled 
Purpose: Identifies the assigned Approval Number. 
Processing Rules: Required on reversals for matching information to the original 
purchase.  If it is included in a Purchase Request, then the 
Purchase Request is considered preauthorized, and BUYPASS 
does not go out for authorization. 
 In the case of an Authorization Only Reversal, this element—
present in the original transaction—must be present and identical 
in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction.  (Note:  The 
Authorization Only Reversal transaction enables a merchant to 
reverse the following credit card transactions within required 
timeframes:  POS Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“3”]); POS Mail/Phone Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“B”]); and CAT Authorization Only [Transaction Type code “5”]). 
Valid Codes/Values: Any alphanumeric representation, including spaces

definitions.name: Block Number
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 11 Name: Block Number 
Character Type:  N Maximum Length: 3 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of three digits 
Purpose: Identifies the specific proprietary or public key data block requested 
by a device or sent by the host. 
Processing Rules: The host always uses a Block Number to track the data block it 
sends in an Electronic Mail response and a CA Public Key File 
Load response.  If response processing is interrupted, the host 
knows the Block Number for the last complete data block sent in 
the response. 
 A device is not required to track the Block Number it receives in 
an Electronic Mail response.  If it is required to do so, and 
processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device 
can reinstate transmission of the interrupted data block using that 
Block Number in the next Electronic Mail request it sends to the 
host. 
 A device always uses a Block Number to track the data block it 
sends in a Proprietary Data Load request.  If request processing is 
interrupted, the host knows the Block Number for the last 
complete data block sent in the request. 
 A device is required to track the Block Number it receives in a CA 
Public Key File Load response.  If CA Public Key File Load 
processing between the host and device is interrupted, the device 
reinstates transmission of the interrupted data block using that 
Block Number in the next request it sends to the host. 
Valid Codes/Values: Codes Description 
000 The host sends the first data block for CA 
Public Key File Load. 
000 The device sends this value indicating the 
last block of site / fuel volume data is being 
sent in the Proprietary Data Load request. 
001 The host restarts data block processing, 
and sends the block that was Block No. 1 in 
the Electronic Mail response as the next 
block. 
 <specific Block No.> The device can request a particular block by 
sending that Block Number in the next 
Electronic Mail request or CA Public Key 
File Load request. 
 
 
  
--- PAGE 364 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-31

definitions.name: Card Discretionary Block Data
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 12 Name: Card Discretionary 
Block Data 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 51 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to 51 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies the card’s expiration date and/or discretionary data. 
Processing Rules: The format varies, depending on the application. 
 If the Account Number is obtained from a Track 2 card reader, 
instead of being manually keyed, the Account Number and Card 
Discretionary Block Data should consist of all data read from the 
card between, but not including, the Start Sentinel and End 
Sentinel.  Account Number is considered the data before the = 
character, and Card Discretionary Block Data is considered the 
data after the = character.  The = character is used instead of a 
Field Separator. 
If the Account Number is obtained from a Track 1 card reader 
(credit cards only), instead of being manually keyed, the Account 
Number and Card Discretionary Block Data should consist of all 
unaltered data read from the card between, but not including, the 
Start Sentinel and End Sentinel.  Account Number is considered 
the data before the first ^ character, and Card Discretionary Block 
Data is considered the data after the first ^ character.  The ^ 
character is used instead of a Field Separator. 
 Account Number and Card Discretionary Block Data combined do 
not exceed 76 characters for Track 1 or 37 characters for Track 2. 
Note: Track data placed in the combined data elements of 
Account Number and Card Discretionary Block Data cannot 
exceed the total length of those data elements 
 For either TransArmor processing method, the expiration date 
must be included here.  The expiration date is stored for follow-on 
transactions associated with a Token. 
 Real Time Account Updater: 
 When a merchant receives Account Updater Expiration Date (New 
Expiration Date) in the original transaction response in the Real 
Time Account Updater Response Segment – Segment 155, the 
merchant can send either the new expiration date or the original 
expiration date in the ‘Follow-on’ transactions in this Card 
Discretionary Block Data field. 
 A merchant should send the Expiration Date corresponding to the 
original PAN or the new PAN / the original or the new TransArmor 
Token that is being sent in the cardholder Account Number field – 
Data Element 2 in the Standard Message Data Segment 100. 
 
--- PAGE 365 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-32 
 In the event of a ‘Retry’ of a ‘Follow-on’ transaction (Reversals, 
Completions, Cancellations, Void of Merchandise Return, and 
Timeout reversals) by the merchant, the merchant should use the 
same credentials for the retry as were used in the initial attempt.  
 Refer to Appendix AD – Real Time Account Updater for more 
details. 
Valid Codes/Values: For a card whose number has been manually entered, the 
expiration date is in MMYY format, and the other required data 
depends upon the application. 
 Note: For all authorizations, merchants must send a value even 
for expired cards. 
 For a Certegy (Formerly Telecredit) transaction, the information 
consists of the 2-character alphabetical State Code (See 
Appendix D.  Valid State Codes.) and the 6-character birth date 
(MMDDYY). 
 If a driver's license number is used as identification for a SCAN 
(ETC) transaction, the information consists of the 2-character 
alphabetical State Code (See Appendix D.  Valid State Codes.). 
 For either TransArmor processing method, the expiration date 
must be included here.  The expiration date is stored for follow-on 
transactions associated with a Token. 
 For a Comdata Express Code or Check request (card type code

Number: 14 Name: Card Type 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 3 bytes 
 
Note: See also the description for Element No. 78, Prompt Code. 
Representation: Fixed length of three alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: In the case of a Table Load response, this code identifies a card 
type the device accepts or a specific feature the device performs.. 
 In the case of a financial transaction, this code identifies the card 
used in the transaction. 
 In the case of a special transaction, this code identifies the type of 
requested data. 
Processing Rules: Must be a valid Card Type code. 
 In the case of a Table Load response, the host sends this code 
multiple times to the device instructing the device about which 
cards to accept and which features to perform. 
 In the case of a financial transaction, the device sends this code to 
the host as part of the 4-character Prompt Code. 
 In the case of a special transaction, the device sends this code to 
the host as a 3-character Prompt Code requesting specific data. 
Valid Codes/Values: For a list of valid entries, please see Appendix E.  Valid Card Type 
Codes.

Number: 24 Name: Data Type Indicator 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 1 byte 
 
Representation: Fixed length of one alphanumeric character 
Purpose: Identifies specific characteristics of the following data in a host 
response. 
Processing Rules: Required for TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization. 
 Required for EMV CA Public Key File Load 
 
Valid Codes/Values: Code Description 
 # Identifies the Merchant Data Segment (No. DL1). 
 ! Identifies the Dial String Data Segment (No. DL2). 
 : Identifies the Date and Time Data Segment (No. 
DL3). 
 @ Identifies the Software Dial Load Data Segment 
(No. DL4). 
 $ Identifies the Software IP Load Data Segment (No. 
DL5). 
 \ Identifies the Store and Forward Data Segment 
(No. DL6). 
 & Indicates that a new Key and Key ID are being 
returned to a device using TransArmor PKI 
Encryption and Tokenization. 
 & For EMV, indicates that a block of a new CA Public 
Key file is being returned to the device. 
 K Indicates that a new Key and Key ID are being 
returned to a device using TransArmor PKI 
Encryption and Tokenization 
 ^ Identifies the Supplemental Terminal Data Segment 
(No. DL7) 
 % Identifies EMV Floor Limits Segment (No. DL8)

constraints.representation: Fixed length of one alphanumeric character

catalogRules.title: Segment DL1 uses NO Field Separators; instead it is self-delimited by a Data Type Indicator ('#', field 1) and an End-of-Data Indicator ('~', last field) — a distinct delimiting convention from the numbered segments (85/84 Segment Type/Length pair)

Segment DL7 is identified by the special character '^' (Data Type Indicator, Element 24) but, UNLIKE Segments DL1-DL6, does NOT use an End-of-Data Indicator; instead it uses a Segment Length Indicator (Element 84) to frame the segment, matching the pattern used by numbered segments (100-157) rather than the DL1-DL6 marker convention

Data Type Indicator is fixed value '%' (Element 24); Segment Length Indicator (Element 84, 3 digits) is EXCLUSIVE of the Data Type Indicator's length, same hybrid framing convention as Segment DL7 (no End-of-Data Indicator)

definitions.name: Encrypted PIN Block Data
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 33 Name: Encrypted PIN Block 
Data 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 36 bytes 
 
Representation: For DUKPT PIN encryption, this is a 16- to 20-byte Key Serial 
Number (KSN) plus a 16-byte PIN block. 
Purpose: Required for debit and EBT. 
 It is not required for a completion. 
 Note: Refer to chapter 6, “PIN Encryption,” for composition of 
PIN block. 
Processing Rules: Customer-keyed, must be encrypted using DUKPT.  If not 
included in a request, insert a Field Separator. 
 For EMV offline PIN validated debit transactions, the 16-byte PIN 
block portion of this data element contains either a PIN or all F’s, 
otherwise the transaction will decline as “invalid transaction”. 
Valid Codes/Values: PIN block composition is validated by hardware PIN encryption 
devices.  If composition is invalid or the device is out-of-sync with 
BUYPASS, the transaction is declined.

Number: 41 Name: Fuel Purchase Amount

subtracting the discount and/or coupon amount from the sum of 
fuel products in Product Amount (No. 76).

applied to the nonfuel amount.

definitions.name: Message Format Version Identifier
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 55 Name: Message Format 
Version Identifier 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 6 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of six alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies the type and release version of message format. 
Processing Rules: All Financial Transaction Request messages, Totals Request 
messages, Loyalty Card Request messages, and Electronic Mail 
Request messages contain this data element in Field No. 1.  It 
originates at the device. 
 For Financial Transaction Requests, the following data element 
and data segment always follow this data element: 
• Element No. 63, Number of Segments 
• Data Segment No. 100, Standard Message Data Segment 
 plus none, one, or more of the following data segments: 
• Data Segment No. 101, Fleet Data Segment 
• Data Segment No. 102, Product Code Data Segment 
• Data Segment No. 103, EBT Data Segment 
• Data Segment No. 104, Purchase Card Data Segment 
• Data Segment No. 111, Variable Information Data Segment 
 For Financial Transaction Responses, the following data segment 
can follow the last data element in the message: 
• Additional Information Data Segment (Data Segment No. 112) 
 For Totals Request messages, the following data element and 
data segment always follow this data element; 
• Element No. 63, Number of Segments 
• Data Segment No. 105, Totals Data Segment 
 For Loyalty Card Request messages, the following data element 
and data segment always follow this data element; 
• Element No. 63, Number of Segments 
• Data Segment No. 108, Loyalty Card Data Segment 
 For Electronic Mail Request messages, the following data element 
and data segment always follow this data element; 
• Element No. 63, Number of Segments 
• Data Segment No. 109, Electronic Mail Data Segment

definitions.name: Nonfuel Amount
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 58 Name: Nonfuel Amount 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 8 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to eight digits with two assumed decimal 
places 
 Note: A maximum length of 8 bytes is allowed for American 
Express cards only.  A maximum length of 7 bytes is 
allowed for all other card types. 
Purpose: Identifies the transaction’s dollar amount that is not a fuel, tax, or 
cash amount. 
Processing Rules: For a stored value card activation transaction, this data contains 
the activation amount. 
 For a stored value card deactivation transaction, this data contains 
the deactivation amount. 
 For a stored value card recharge transaction, this data contains 
the recharge amount. 
 For a transaction involving only a nonfuel purchase and discounts 
and/or coupons, this amount is the net amount derived by 
subtracting the discount and/or coupon amount from the sum of 
nonfuel products in Product Amount (No. 76). 
 For a transaction involving fuel and nonfuel amounts together with 
 discounts and/or coupons, the discounts and/or coupons are first 
 applied to the nonfuel amount. 
Valid Codes/Values: 1–99999999

definitions.name: Number of Segments
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 63 Name: Number of Segments 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 2 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to two digits 
Purpose: Identifies the number of BUYPASS-defined data segments 
included in the Financial Transaction Request, Totals Request, 
Loyalty Card Transaction Request, and Electronic Mail Request. 
Processing Rules: It originates at the device. 
 Financial Transaction Requests:  This data element is always 
followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains Data Segment No. 
100, Standard Message Data Segment, plus Data Section No. 3 
which contains none, one, or more of the of the input data 
segments listed in Chapter 12. 
 Loyalty Card Transaction Requests:  This data element is 
always followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains Data 
Segment No. 100, Standard Message Data Segment, plus Data 
Section No. 3 which contains Data Segment No. 108, Loyalty 
Card Data Segment, and Data Segment 114, SKU Data Segment. 
 ECA/ TeleCheck® Service Transaction Requests:  This data 
element is always followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains 
Data Segment No. 100, Standard Message Data Segment, plus 
Data Section No. 3 which contains Data Segment No. 110, Check 
Data Segment, and Data Segment 111, Variable Information Data 
Segment. 
 Totals Requests:  This data element is always followed by Data 
Segment No. 105, Totals Data Segment. 
 Electronic Mail Requests:  This data element is always followed 
by Data Section No. 2, which contains Data Segment No. 109, 
Electronic Mail Data Segment. 
 Communications Test Requests:  This data element is always 
followed by Data Section No. 2 which contains Element No. 120, 
Network Management Message. 
 TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization:  This data 
element is used for a Key and Key ID Load.  In the requests, it is 
always followed by Data Section No. 2, which contains Data 
Segment No. 116, TransArmor Load Data Segment. 
 
Valid Codes/Values: The value of this field, call it N, indicates that the transaction will 
 have the 100 segment + N-1 of the input segments listed in 
 Chapter 12. 
 
 
--- PAGE 389 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-56

definitions.name: Product Code
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 77 Name: Product Code 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 3 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of three digits 
Purpose: Identifies the type of product in Data Segment No. 102, Product 
Code Data Segment or Data Segment No. 157, Adjusted Product 
Code Data Segment.  
 In the case of a Proprietary Load Response (Prompt Code 904), 
the first instance identifies the type of product which is eligible for 
discount, and the second instance identifies the corresponding 
discount product code to send in Data Segment No. 102, Product 
Code Data Segment. 
Processing Rules: This data element, along with the following data elements, is 
repeated for up to a maximum of 10 products in Data Segment 
No. 102 or Data Segment No. 157: 
• Unit of Measure (No. 106) 
• Quantity (No. 81) 
• Unit Price (No. 107) 
• Product Amount (No. 76) 
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel 
purchase. 
 When a device uses a Dynamic Card Table, only the product 
codes defined in the table are valid for transaction processing.  
 In the case of a Proprietary Load Response (Host Discount Data, 
Prompt Code 904), the value in the second or third positions of the 
Product Code may contain a wild card character of *.  If that 
occurs, any digit is allowed in that position.  For example, if the 
value is 01*, product codes 010, 011, 012, 013, 014, 015, 016, 
017, 018 and 019 are all available for discount. 
Valid Codes/Values: Please refer to Appendix F.  Valid Payment Systems Product 
Codes, for lists of valid codes.

definitions.name: Prompt Code
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 78 Name: Prompt Code 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 4 bytes 
 
Note: See also the description for Element No. 14, Card Type. 
Representation: Variable length of three or four alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: In the case of a financial transaction, this is a 4-character Prompt 
Code that identifies the transaction’s Transaction Type (one 
character) and Card Type (three characters). 
--- PAGE 394 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-61 
 In the case of a special transaction, this is a 3-character Prompt 
Code that identifies requested special data (3-character Card 
Type). 
Processing Rules: Must be a valid Transaction Type code and/or Card Type code. 
 In the case of a financial transaction, a device transmits a 4-
character Prompt Code when the transaction is initiated. 
 In the case of a special transaction, a device transmits a 3-
character Prompt Code (3-character Card Type) for a special 
transaction when the transaction is initiated. 
 In the case of an Authorization Only Reversal, this element—
present in the original transaction—must be present and identical 
in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction.  (Note:  The 
Authorization Only Reversal transaction enables a merchant to 
reverse the following credit card transactions within required 
timeframes:  POS Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“3”]); POS Mail/Phone Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“B”]); and CAT Authorization Only [Transaction Type code “5”]). 
 Signature Debit eligible transactions must be sent with a Credit 
Prompt Code, and NOT a Debit Prompt Code. 
 In EMV transactions, if ‘D’ is returned in response, then 
subsequent transactions i.e. completion or void or reversal must 
be sent as credit. This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data 
Segment 100: Data Element 78) of the subsequent transaction. 
 In EMV transactions, if ‘S’ is returned in response, then 
subsequent transactions i.e. completion or void or reversal must 
be sent as debit. This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data 
Segment 100: Data Element 78) of the subsequent transaction.  
Valid Codes/Values: In the case of a financial transaction, position no. 1 is the 
Transaction Type (For a list of valid entries, please see Appendix 
G.  Valid Transaction Type Codes.); and position nos. 2–4 are the 
Card Type (For a list of valid entries, please see Appendix E.  Valid 
Card Type Codes.). 
 In the case of a special transaction, position nos. 1–3 are the Card 
Type (For a list of valid entries, please see Appendix E.  Valid 
Card Type Codes.) that identifies requested special data.

constraints.representation: Variable length of three or four alphanumeric characters

• Unit Price (No. 107) 
• Product Amount (No. 76)

places and 10 represents the quantity of 10. 
 34170 = 4.170, where 3 is the number of assumed decimal places 
and 4170 represents the quantity of 4.170.

POS Purchase Example.

Representation: Fixed length of one alphanumeric character 
Purpose: For financial transactions, it identifies an approval with

mail retrieval pending, decline with electronic mail retrieval 
pending, approved with electronic mail retrieval pending and 
proprietary data pending, declined with electronic mail retrieval

identifies one of the following: 
• The transaction is an approved TransArmor PKI Encryption 
and Tokenization transaction. 
• The transaction is a rejected TransArmor PKI Encryption and 
Tokenization transaction. 
• The merchant is not a TransArmor merchant.

• The transaction is an approved EMV transaction. 
• The transaction is a rejected EMV transaction.

definitions.name: Segment Length
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 84 Name: Segment Length 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 4 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of three or four digits 
 Note: Segment Length has a length of four digits in the following 
seven instances only: 
• EBT Data Segment (No. 103) 
• SKU Data Segment (No. 114) 
• Print Data Segment (No. 115) 
• Proprietary Data Load Segment (No. 118) 
• Print Data 2 Segment (No. 120) 
• EMV Request Data Segment (No.130) 
• EMV Response Data Segment (No. 131) 
Purpose: Identifies the length of the segment in which it appears. 
Processing Rules:  This figure is calculated using the lengths of all data elements in  
    the segment plus all Field Separators/Product Data Field   
    Delimiters related to those elements.  (Please refer to chapter 12,  
    “Data Segment Formats,” for additional information about specific  
    data segments—including their composition, data element   
    lengths, Field Separators, and Product Data Field Delimiters.) 
 Note: Segment Length can only have a length of 4 digits when 
transmitting the following Data Segments.  It cannot have 
a length of 4 digits when sending any other segment. 
• EBT Data Segment (No. 103) 
• SKU Data Segment (No. 114) 
• Print Data Segment (No. 115) 
• Proprietary Data Load Segment (No. 118) 
• Print Data 2 Segment (No. 120) 
• EMV Request Data Segment (No.130)

definitions.name: Sequence Number
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 86 Name: Sequence Number 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 6 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of six digits 
Purpose: Note: Identifies a transaction for the life of the transaction. 
Sequence Number must persist in all the subsequent transactions 
that are associated with the initial authorization request. 
 In the case of a preauthorized transaction, the Sequence Number 
in the Purchase/Capture identifies the Sequence Number in the 
transaction’s Authorization Only request. 
Processing Rules: Each transaction has a unique Sequence Number.  It is included 
on all transaction types, and originates at the device. 
 In the case of a preauthorized transaction, the Sequence Number 
in the Purchase/Capture is the same Sequence Number as in the 
transaction’s Authorization Only request. 
 In the case of a purchase reversal/void or time-out reversal 
transaction, the Sequence Number must be the same as in the 
original transaction request. 
 In the case of an Authorization Only Reversal, this element—
present in the original transaction—must be present and identical 
in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction.  (Note:  The 
Authorization Only Reversal transaction enables a merchant to 
reverse the following credit card transactions within required 
timeframes:  POS Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“3”]); POS Mail/Phone Authorization Only [Transaction Type code 
“B”]); and CAT Authorization Only [Transaction Type code “5”]). 
 For TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization, this element is 
included in a new data segment (No. 116 [TransArmor Load Data 
Segment]). 
Valid Codes/Values: 000001–999999 
 100000-199999   
  
--- PAGE 403 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-70 
Note: This limited sequence number range (100000-199999) 
consists of the only allowed values when using the Multithreaded 
Dial Protocol Communications header for a CAPK File Load for 
the ATL105 message format

Other Reserved for future use.

Number: 102 Name: Terminal Identifier 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 22 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length up to 22 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies the transaction device by Device Type, State Code 
(ANSI® Code), BUYPASS Merchant Number, and Device 
Number. 
Processing Rules: Required for all transactions and messages. 
 The Terminal Identifier must be assigned by and set up at 
BUYPASS. 
 Note: In the case of a Table Load Request, Phone Load 
Request, Date and Time Load Request, or Software Load 
Request, the field length is 13 bytes; otherwise, the field 
length is a maximum of 22 bytes. 
 For the TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization Load 
Request, the first two characters (Device Type) of this element’s 
value must be “++” regardless of the actual device type. 
 For the EMV Key Load Request, the first two characters (Device 
Type) of this element’s value must be “+*” regardless of the actual 
device type. 
Valid Codes/Values: Device Type (Pos. Nos. 1–2) 
 Any valid 2-character Device Type assigned by BUYPASS 
personnel. 
 For the TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization Load 
Request, this element’s value must be “++” regardless of the 
actual device type. 
 For the EMV Key Load Request, this element’s value must be “+*” 
regardless of the actual device type. 
 State Code (Pos. Nos. 3–4) 
 Any valid 2-character State Code (ANSI® Code).  Please see 
Appendix D.  Valid State Codes, for a list of valid ANSI® Code 
entries. 
 BUYPASS Merchant Number (Starts immediately in Pos. No. 5.) 
 Any valid 6- to 15-character BUYPASS Merchant Number 
assigned by BUYPASS personnel.  The Device Number 
immediately follows the BUYPASS Merchant Number. 
 Note: If using TransArmor, the first 6 digits of the Merchant 
Number are used in Error! Reference source not found..  P
lease refer to the description of Element No. 2 (Account 
Number) for additional information. 
Device Number (Starts immediately after the BUYPASS 
Merchant Number.)

definitions.name: Totals Date
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 105 Name: Totals Date 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 6 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of six digits 
Purpose: Identifies the date for which totals are being requested or the date 
for which totals and an end-of-day are being requested. 
Processing Rules: The customer assigns this information.  Totals cannot be 
requested for a date prior to the third most recent date with 
activity. 
 Note: The value of this field in a Totals Response can be 
different than the value sent in the Totals Request. 
Valid Codes/Values: Request Response Description 
 MMDDYY YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for a 
specified settlement date. 
 111111 111111 Identifies a request for totals for the 
period of time since the last 999999 
code was used. 
 222222 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
current settlement date; ends the 
current settlement date; and rolls the 
date to the next settlement date. 
 333333 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
most recent date with activity. 
 444444 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
second most recent date with 
activity. 
 555555 YYMMDD Identifies a request for totals for the 
third most recent date with activity. 
 999999 999999 Identifies a request to clear all totals 
since the last 999999 code was 
used.  Used with the 111111 code.

definitions.sourceText:
Number: 107 Name: Unit Price 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 9 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to nine digits with a maximum of three 
assumed decimal places 
Purpose: Identifies the price per Unit of Measure of a product in Data 
Segment No. 102, Product Code Data Segment or Data Segment 
No. 157, Adjusted Product Code Data Segment. 
Processing Rules: The leading number indicates the number of assumed decimal 
places.  There is a maximum number of three assumed decimal 
places. 
 This data element, along with the following data elements, is 
repeated for up to 10 products in Data Segment No. 102, Product 
Code Data Segment or Data Segment No. 157, Adjusted Product 
Code Data Segment: 
• Product Code (No. 77) 
• Unit of Measure (No. 106) 
• Quantity (No. 81) 
• Product Amount (No. 76) 
Valid Codes/Values: 000000.000–999999.999 
 For an example of this data element, please see Appendix B.  
POS Purchase Example.

Purpose: Identifies the data in a Variable Information Data Segment.

existingBusinessRequirements.title: The Consumer Bill Payment/Purchase Repayment indicator value 'CB' shall be used only for Visa transactions, and value 'IR' shall be used only for MasterCard transactions.
For MasterCard Purchase Repayment transactions, the merchant shall submit the Installment Payment Indicator value 'I' in Segment 111 Table ID 013 (Special Payments Indicator Information).
For MasterCard Purchase Repayment transactions, the merchant shall submit the Merchant Name in Segment 111 Table ID 047 (Soft Descriptor) in the format 'Installment Provider name*Merchant name'.

A decline for a merchant not registered for the Purchase Repayment program shall return Merchant Advice Code 22 ('Merchant does not qualify for product code') when the merchant sent the Merchant Advice Code acceptance indicator (Table ID 049 Sub Table 07 = 'Y').
A country reference in Table ID 59 shall use a valid three-digit country code from the Appendix AC list.
The Table ID 59 country code shall identify the country in which the acquiring institution resides, consistent with the merchant/acquirer configuration.
Real Time Account Updater applies only to card-not-present transactions from a participating, registered/certified acquirer/merchant that are Credential-on-File, Installment, or Recurring payments.

A participating merchant shall send the Account Updater Request Indicator (Segment 111, Table ID 060, Sub Table ID 01) as the trigger on Installment, Recurring, and Credential-on-File request messages.
An estimated/initial authorization request for a permitted merchant shall include the estimated authorization indicator (Acquirer Trace Data Sub Table ID 09) when the final amount is unknown.

An incremental authorization request shall follow an estimated/initial authorization, must not resend the estimated-authorization indicator, and must carry the same Sequence Number, Transaction Identifier, and Terminal Transaction Number (Segment 111 Table ID 63) as the original estimated/initial request.

Sub Table 18 (Purchase Restriction Method) is mandatory on MasterCard Enhanced EMV Fleet (Product IDs MCF/MGF) Authorization, Pre-Authorization, and Completion transactions, and must not be sent for any other transaction; if omitted, Buypass defaults to Visa No Restrictions supported.
POS Entry Mode Element 113 shall contain a valid two-digit PAN Entry Mode followed by a valid one-digit Terminal Capability Mode.
PAN Entry Mode shall use a source-defined value consistent with the card-entry method and transaction context.
Terminal Capability Mode shall reflect the POS PIN, EMV, contactless, or mPOS capability hierarchy.
POS Entry Mode shall persist across lifecycle transactions except for source-defined exceptions, including PAN mode 90 referenced by a completion or void using mode 02.
Entry Mode 10, 82, and terminal capability mode 3 shall be used only in their source-defined card, network, and mPOS contexts.
Tokenized Segment 100 transactions shall use a POS Entry Mode that identifies the token presentment mode.
National POS Condition Code shall contain the source-defined ten-position structure: terminal class, presentation type, security condition, and terminal type.
Terminal class and terminal type positions shall use valid Appendix Q values consistent with the physical or digital POS channel.
Presentation positions shall correctly identify customer/card presence, mail/telephone order, preauthorization, retention capability, and re-presentment state.
Security Condition position shall use valid values for no concern, suspected fraud, verified identification, or electronic commerce digital signature.
POS Condition Code shall be consistent with Segment 100 Prompt Code, entry mode, transaction lifecycle, and eWIC/channel context.

A merchant participating in the Online Refund/Refund Authorization program must send the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator in Variable Information Table ID 32 Sub Table 11 on a Merchandise Return transaction requesting online authorization; a merchant not wanting online approval must not send it.
The Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator value must be 'Y' for Visa, MasterCard, Amex, and Discover.
When the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator is present on a Merchandise Return, it must also be included in the subsequent reversal/follow-up transactions and in Timeout Reversals.
Amex SafeKey transactions shall be sent with indicator 'SK' followed by 56 bytes of SafeKey data in base64 format; when the first 28 bytes are not applicable, they shall be space-filled.
When storing a credential for the first time, Variable Information Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 shall carry Value 'I' (Initial), whether sent as a $0.00 Account Verification or an amount-due transaction.

A merchant-initiated recurring stored-credential transaction shall be identified as 'R', use Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'C' (Subsequent), POS Entry Mode '10', and include Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'M' (Merchant Initiated).

A merchant-initiated installment stored-credential transaction shall be identified as 'I', use Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'C', POS Entry Mode '10', include Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'M', and must not send CVV2 data.

A merchant-initiated unscheduled stored-credential transaction shall not be identified as Installment or Recurring, and shall include Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'M', Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'C', and POS Entry Mode '10'.

A cardholder-initiated recurring or installment stored-credential transaction shall use Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'I' and Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'C' (Cardholder Initiated) with the original POS Entry Mode on the initial transaction.

The Visa/Amex Transaction ID and Discover Network Reference Number returned on the initial stored-credential authorization response shall be stored and included on all subsequent merchant-initiated transactions using that credential.

definitions.name: Partial Approval Indicator
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 121 Name: Partial Approval 
Indicator 
Character Type: N Maximum Length: 1 byte 
 
Representation: Fixed length of 1 digit 
Purpose: Indicates whether or not a merchant supports credit/debit/fleet 
Partial Approvals. 
Processing Rules: Required on all transactions. 
Valid Codes/Values: Value Description 
0 Not specified (default)/Not supported 
 This value is the default value. 
 If the Merchant does not support credit/debit/fleet 
Partial Approvals, then this value is transmitted. 
 1 Supported 
This value indicates that the Merchant supports 
credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval transactions. 
If the Merchant transmits this value with a 
transaction—and the corresponding network 
supports credit/debit/fleet Partial Approval 
transactions—the network can approve an amount 
that is less than the amount in the Authorization 
request; and BUYPASS will send a Partial Approval 
response. 
The network may return a card balance that is 
printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. 
 5 This value indicates that the Merchant only 
supports the receipt of the card balance, not Partial 
Approval transaction processing. 
The network may return a card balance that is 
printed on the customer’s copy of the receipt. 
Note: This value is only supported for American 
Express prepaid cards. 
Note: Support for Partial Authorization is mandatory for all card brands. Data Element 121 ( 
Partial Approval Indicator) should be populated correctly for all card present transactions, 
showing that the terminal is capable of partial authorization responses. 
Note: For American Express transactions, Merchants sending transaction request amount as 
‘zero’ and using values ‘1’ or ‘5’ for Prepaid card balances, will not be receiving the card balance 
back in response.

Number: 122 Name: MICR Data

Representation: Variable length of up to 50 alphanumeric characters

 If MICR data is greater than 50 bytes, include the first 50 bytes 
(from left to right) in this field.   
 Note: MICR Data is also included in Account Number (Element 
No. 2) of the Standard Message Data Segment (Segment 
No. 100). 
If MICR data > 50 bytes and the prompt code is ECA/

constraints.representation: Variable length of up to 50 alphanumeric characters

catalogRules.title: MICR Data (Element 122) is required, alphanumeric, maximum 50 bytes, and required on all check transactions; when raw MICR data exceeds 50 bytes, only the first 50 bytes (left to right) are placed here and the remainder is expected in Extended MICR Data (Element 137), whose hosting data segment is not confirmed by the extracted Segment 110 table

Two MICR encodings are documented in narrative text: Full MICR Line TAC format (example T999999999A999999999999999999C999999) and Full MICR Line RAW TOAD format (symbol substitution using T, O, A, D); Alternate MICR IND = 'Y' signals RAW TOAD/ALB1 format, but no machine-checkable grammar beyond the example and the 50-byte length limit is given

MICR Data (Element 122) is cross-referenced from Account Number (Element 2) of the Standard Message Data Segment (100); the extract states MICR data 'is also included' there but does not state a byte-identity or co-validation rule between the two representations

definitions.name: WIC Product Data
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 154 Name: WIC Product Data 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 3001 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to 3,001 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies data unique to eWIC transactions. 
Processing Rules: Appears in EBT Data Segment (Segment No. 103). 
 Composed of two or more of the following subelements: 
• Total Length 
• One or more of the following: 
• Earliest WIC Benefit Expiration Date 
• WIC Prescription Balance Information 
• WIC UPC Exception/Denial Information 
• WIC UPC Purchase Information 
Earliest WIC Benefit Expiration Date is included in the eWIC 
Balance Inquiry Response, eWIC Authorization Response, and 
eWIC Purchase Completion Response. 
WIC Prescription Balance is included in the eWIC Balance Inquiry 
Response, eWIC Authorization Response, eWIC Purchase 
Completion Response. 
For WIC purchases involving fruits and vegetables via the Cash 
Value Benefit (CVB), please set the Quantity equal to the price in 
the WIC Purchase Information. 
WIC UPC Exception/Denial Information is included in the eWIC 
Purchase Completion Response, and eWIC Voucher Clear 
Response. 
In cases where the WIC Purchase price exceeds the value set by 
the state (and provided in the Approved Product List [APL] file), an 
exception record is returned in the WIC Product Data field.  The 
exception record reflects both the approved and original prices for 
the transaction.  The total transaction amount (Settlement 
Amount) is adjusted to reflect the total price adjustments, and is 
returned in the Approved Amount field.

Number: 155 Name: Key ID 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 11 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of 11 alphanumeric bytes 
Purpose: Used in TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization to identify 
the Key ID associated with the encryption Key included in Element 
No. 157 (Key Data) in the TransArmor Load Response. 
Processing Rules: Required in the TransArmor Load Response. 
 Once requested and approved, this Key ID must be used for all 
subsequent TransArmor transactions from this device. 
Valid Codes/Values: Any valid Key ID (including CA Key ID that is returned in response 
to a Signing Key request).

definitions.sourceText:
Number: 164 Name: EBT Program Data 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 267 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable maximum length of up to 267 alphanumeric characters 
 It is composed of two subelements: 
• Total Length (Fixed length of 3 digits; appears only once.) 
• Program Data (Variable maximum length of 264 alphanumeric 
bytes; 1–6 subelements of a maximum variable length of 44 
bytes each.) 
 The total length of the element is based on the number of 
Program Data subelements sent/received. 
Purpose: Identifies additional transaction data unique to EBT programs. 
Processing Rules: This element is transmitted in Data Segment No. 103, EBT Data 
Segment. 
 It is composed of two subelements: 
• Total Length (Fixed length of 3 digits; appears only once.) 
• Program Data (Variable maximum length of 264 alphanumeric 
bytes; 1–6 subelements of a maximum variable length of 44 
bytes each.) 
 The total length of the element is based on the number of 
Program Data subelements sent/received. 
Valid Codes/Values: This element contains two subelements: 
• Total Length (Fixed length of 3 digits; appears only once.) 
• Program Data (Variable maximum length of 264 alphanumeric 
bytes; 1–6 subelements of a maximum variable length of 44 
bytes each.) 
 The following tables describe the content of these two 
subelements:

definitions.name: Start Date or End Date
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 165 Name: Start Date or End Date 
Character Type: N Length: 8 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of eight digits (CCYYMMDD) 
Purpose: Identifies the start date or end date the device uses custom 
receipt text or host discount data. 
Processing Rules: Appears in Proprietary Data Load Segment (Segment No. 118). 
 When it appears as a Start Date and contains 00000000 this 
indicates the data is used immediately. 
 When it appears as an End Date and contains 99999999 this 
indicates the data is used until further notice.   
 Used with Element No. 166, Start Time or End Time. 
Valid Codes/Values: Code Description 
 00–99 Century 
 00–99 Year of the century 
 01–12 Month of the year 
 01-31 Day of the month 
 00000000 Start immediately 
 99999999 No end date

When Prompt Code is 904 (Host Discount Data, response only), fields 14-27 are: Host Discount Timestamp (179, 12), Number of Discounts (171, 2), then a repeated block of Start Date (165,8), Start Time (166,4), End Date (165,8), End Time (166,4), BUYPASS Card Type (173,4), Card BIN Range Beginning (183,12), Card BIN Range Ending (184,12), Product Code (77,3), Product Discount Amount (172,5), Product Code (77,3), Discount Quantity Limit (185,3), Discount Program Description (186,15), for a total variable length not to exceed 3,600 bytes

definitions.name: EMV Chip Data
definitions.sourceText:
Number: 190 Name: EMV Chip Data 
Character Type: ANSB Maximum Length: 999 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of 999 characters, preceded by three digit length 
indicator 
 All fields after the table length are in binary format. 
Purpose: Identifies the data sent in the EMV card to terminal interface. 
Processing Rules: Required in all EMV transactions. 
 EMV data elements include a series of TLV (Tag/Length/Value) 
combinations which are required for processing EMV transactions. 
 All data elements must contain the exact values that were present on 
the card to terminal interface. 
 If the same data element appears several times on the card to 
terminal interface, this field must contain the last value that was 
present on the card to terminal interface during the transaction. 
 Note: For the EMV transaction to be processed properly, the 
Application ID (AID) TLV (tag 9F06) or Dedicated File Name (tag 84) 
must be included in Data Element No. 190 (EMV Chip Data). 
Note: Tag ‘5A’ (PAN) and Tag ‘57’ (Track 2 equivalent data) must not 
be included in Data Element 190 — EMV Chip Data. 
Valid Codes/Values: The components of EMV data elements are described below: 
Component Name:  Tag 
Each sub element or Tag can be either one or two bytes long.  To 
determine the length, check the last five bits of the first byte, if they 
are all on (1) the tag of the sub element is two bytes long, including 
the current byte. 
Example 1: Tag x’9F10’ is a two byte tag - the last five bits of 
the first byte (x’9F’) are all ones. 
Example 2: Tag x’72’ is a one byte tag - the last five bits of the 
first byte (x’72’) are not all ones. 
Component Name:  Length (ANSB …127) 
The next one or more bytes are the length indicator of the tag.  To 
determine the number of length bytes used for this inspect the first 
byte of the length field.  If the first bit of the first byte is a 1, the 
remaining bits (next seven) are a binary representation of the number 
of following bytes of the length field.  If the first bit is 0, the remaining 
bits indicate the actual length of the data that follows.  
Example 1: If the length byte is x’0C’, then 12 is the length of 
the data that follows the sub element. 
Example 2: If the tag is x’82’, the length is contained in the next 
byte of the sub element. The value in the length byte 
indicates the number of bytes of data following. 
--- PAGE 472 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
13-139 
Component Name:  Value (ANSB …255) 
The data of each Tag/Length/Value combination is up to 255 bytes 
long, depending on the length of the field specified by the preceding 
length portion of the sub element.  
For an example of this data element, please see Appendix R.  EMV 
Chip Data.

Number: 194 Name: CA Public Key File  
  Block 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 9,999 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of 9,999 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies either the Public Key file in the CA Public Key File Load 
Response or the Error Message. 
Processing Rules: Required in the CA Public Key File Load Response. 
 The CA Public Key File contains all active CA Public Keys that apply 
for processing EMV transactions. 
 The CA Public Key File completely replaces the key file previously 
stored at the device. 
 For an approved EMV load transaction, the maximum length is 9,999 
bytes.

data to construct the CA Public Key File. 
 For a declined EMV load transaction, a message is returned in this 
field and displays at the device. 
Valid Codes/Values: Any valid key. 
 Following are the error codes that are returned in the terminal: 
 Code     Description 
 RQST/CURRENT HASH MATCH Key update not required 
 BLOCK NBR NOT NUMERIC  Key load transaction not  
   successful

   successful

Number: 196 Name: Token Requestor ID 
Character Type: AN Max. Length: 11 bytes 
 
Representation: Fixed length of 11 bytes 
Purpose: Identifies merchant’s Token Requestor ID. 
Processing Rules: This Data Element is used only for Visa/MasterCard payment 
tokenized transactions. 
Valid Codes/Values: Position        Description 
                                               1-11               Token Requestor ID, Left justified, space-filled 
Note: In late 2014, MasterCard introduced the Card on File 
tokenization service and static card on file token type to support 
token payments for e-Commerce merchants that traditionally 
stored credit card numbers.  MasterCard required merchants to 
submit the Token Requestor ID for Card on File tokenized 
transactions.  Effective 8 June 2021, MasterCard renamed the 
Card on File token type to “Static Token” type.  Also, they 
removed the requirement to submit the Token Requestor ID. 
However, if submitted, MasterCard will validate and will decline if 
invalid.  
Merchants are advised not to send the Token Requestor ID if 
submitting a Card on File tokenized transaction/Static Token type.  
Cryptographic Data is still not required for Static Tokens.   
Merchants that submit Secure Element and Cloud-based token 
types are still required to submit the Token Requestor ID along 
with Cryptographic data, if applicable.

Number: 198 Name: Settlement Type 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 1 byte 
 
Representation: Fixed length 1 alphanumeric character. 
Purpose: Identifies how the transaction was processed – Single message 
(debit) or Dual message (credit). 
Processing Rules: Required in the Common AID EMV and non-traditional Signature 
Debit Financial Transaction Response. 
Note: Please check with your First Data Project Manager or 
Relationship Manager for availability of Signature Debit functionality. 
Valid Codes/Values: Following are the values that are returned in the terminal: 
 Value Description 
 D  Transaction was processed Dual message (credit) 
 S  Transaction was processed Single message (debit) 
 X  Transaction was processed Dual message (non-traditional  
   Signature Debit) 
 Note: In EMV transactions, if ‘D’ is returned in response, then 
 subsequent transactions i.e. completion or void or reversal must be 
 sent as credit. This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data 
 segment 100: Data Element 78) of the subsequent transaction. 
   In EMV transactions, if ‘S’ is returned in response, then 
 subsequent transactions i.e. completion or void or reversal must be 
 sent as debit. This will be reflected in the Prompt Code (Data segment 
 100: Data  Element 78) of the subsequent transaction.

August 07, 2026 
13-144

catalogRules.title: TAVV Cryptogram (Element 237, 28 bytes, base64 alphabet a-z/A-Z/0-9/+/=// ) may only be populated by the merchant during the transaction request, not the response

When both MasterCard DSRP cryptogram and SecureCode/Identity Check 3DS AAV are present in the same request, the AAV must be carried in Segment 111 Table ID 36 (UCAF) and the Token/DSRP cryptogram must be carried in Segment 123 Element 237 (TAVV) — the two fields are not interchangeable and both may be required simultaneously

existingBusinessRequirements.title: For Visa token-based transactions combined with 3-D Secure, the TAVV token cryptogram and the 3DS CAVV cryptogram (revised format) shall be populated per the defined Verified-by-Visa-only, Digital-Wallet-only, or combined scenario.

MasterCard AAV cryptogram data shall use Segment 111 Table ID 36 (UCAF Data) while Token/DSRP cryptograms shall use Segment 123 Element 237 (TAVV); when both are present, the UCAF Security Level Code shall be '21' (Channel Encrypted).

For Visa token-based transactions combined with 3-D Secure, the TAVV token cryptogram and the 3DS CAVV cryptogram (revised format) shall be populated per the defined Verified-by-Visa-only, Digital-Wallet-only, or combined scenario.

MasterCard AAV cryptogram data shall use Segment 111 Table ID 36 (UCAF Data) while Token/DSRP cryptograms shall use Segment 123 Element 237 (TAVV); when both are present, the UCAF Security Level Code shall be '21' (Channel Encrypted).

catalogRules.title: Alternate MICR IND, documented in Section 12.9 as Segment 110 field 12 using element number 239, is optional, fixed 1 byte, and its only documented value is 'Y' (Alternate/RAW TOAD MICR format is being sent); this element number is separately defined in the Chapter 13 master element catalog as 'Enhanced Fleet Data' (999 bytes, used by Segment 145). Per SME decision (2026-09-26), both usages are modeled as distinct, segment-scoped entities (element 239 @ Segment 110 vs. element 239 @ Segment 145); this rule intentionally remains REVIEW_REQUIRED by design, not due to a gap

Two MICR encodings are documented in narrative text: Full MICR Line TAC format (example T999999999A999999999999999999C999999) and Full MICR Line RAW TOAD format (symbol substitution using T, O, A, D); Alternate MICR IND = 'Y' signals RAW TOAD/ALB1 format, but no machine-checkable grammar beyond the example and the 50-byte length limit is given

Enhanced Fleet Data (Element 239) is required, max 999 characters, containing one or more sub-segments in <tag><len><data> format, cataloged as: Table 001 (Request Flags, incl. Commercial/Retail Flag), Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Data, product-category-coded, '|'-delimited repeating), Table 004 (Prompt Data, authorizer-specific prompt tokens, '|'-delimited repeating), Table 006 (Money Code Payee Name), Table 007 (Money Code Check Number, required for all Money Code transactions), Table 008 (Cash Advance Limit)

Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Data) product categories are authorizer-specific; a documented list applies to WEX OTR transactions (e.g., ADD, ANFR, BRAK, ... WWFL); other authorizers' category lists are not enumerated in this section

Table 004 (Prompt Data) prompt tokens are authorizer-specific and independently cataloged for Voyager EMV (DF-tag-based), Visa Fleet 2.0, Comdata, WEX OTR, and Conexxus (numeric prompt codes, used by MasterCard Enhanced Fleet EMV); full enumeration of all prompt-token tables is out of scope for this rule catalog pass

Enhanced Fleet Data (Element 239) is required, max 999 characters, cataloged as: Table 001 (Response Flags, incl. Settlement Indicator: CP/DB/DF/RC/RF/FN), Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Limits, NOT present in Comdata responses), Table 003 (Fuel Product Limits, using Appendix F product codes), Table 004 (Prompt Formats, using documented edit masks), Table 005 (Customer Information: name/city/state/account code), Table 010 (Additional Response Data: FNAM/LNAM/ATHN/ACCT/DMSG)

Table 004 (Prompt Formats) uses a documented edit-mask grammar: '?' (re-prompt), 'A'/'B' (alphanumeric, treated identically since 2015-01-02), 'N' (numeric only), 'I' (free format), 'O' (optional response), 'Z' (capture but don't resend), 'T' (data type N=Number/S=String), 'Mn'/'Xn' (min/max), 'Vn' (exact match), 'Pn' (pattern match using @ /# /* /literal)
Table 003 (Fuel Product Limits) uses standard product codes from ATL105 Appendix F (Valid Payment Systems Product Codes) — unlike Table 002's non-fuel category codes

Network Token Data (Element 239) is required, max 999 characters, cataloged as 6 fixed sub-tables: 001 (Network Token, 013-018 bytes), 002 (Expiration Date, fixed 004), 003 (Provisional Fee Indicator, fixed 001), 004 (Input Indicator, fixed 001), 005 (Eligible Indicator, fixed 001), 006 (PAN Indicator, fixed 001)
